Each container has its own localhost
A container is isolated with Linux namespaces, as the article on containers and VMs showed, and one of them is the

. Docker's networking overview describes what that leaves the container with: it "only sees a network interface with an IP address, a gateway, a routing table, DNS services, and other networking details." In our test,
in an Alpine container listed exactly two interfaces:
. The docs say the same about DNS:
"refers to the container's own loopback address." Nothing listens on port 8090 inside the API container, so the connection is refused.
Containers find each other by name on a user-defined network

The default network has a catch. Containers on the default bridge can reach each other by IP, but "they cannot refer to each other by name." On a network you create, "containers can communicate with each other using container IP addresses or container names." Compose does this for you: each service "joins the default network and is both reachable by other containers on that network, and discoverable by its service name." Published ports are for the host, not between containers

fails: inside the renderer, nginx listens on 80.
Your machine has its own name
To reach a service running on your machine, Docker Desktop provides

The fix: use the right address for each direction
Both tabs ran on Docker Desktop for Windows (Engine 29.4) with

tabs.label: ❌ Wrong
tabs.code:
# renderer is on network shop, published with -p 127.0.0.1:8090:80
curl -sI http://localhost:8090 | head -1   # from the laptop
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
docker run --rm --network shop alpine:3.22 \
  wget --spider http://localhost:8090
# Connecting to localhost:8090 ([::1]:8090)
# wget: can't connect to remote host: Connection refused
docker run --rm --network shop alpine:3.22 \
  wget --spider http://renderer:8090
# Connecting to renderer:8090 (172.26.0.2:8090)
# wget: can't connect to remote host (172.26.0.2): Connection refused
docker run --rm alpine:3.22 wget --spider http://renderer
# wget: bad address 'renderer'

tabs.label: ✅ Right
tabs.code:
docker network create shop
# 734fc117d8b054006e86cc64f5f083ca23a9e49c98bf15ca9377e70b1ad805d4
docker run -d --name renderer --network shop \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8090:80 nginx:1.29.8-alpine
# da288351a2d7942fe077e3ca18d35805321e56de114cf2764031414585e9f164
docker run --rm --network shop alpine:3.22 \
  wget --spider http://renderer:80   # name + container port
# Connecting to renderer:80 (172.26.0.2:80)
# remote file exists
docker run --rm alpine:3.22 \
  wget --spider http://host.docker.internal:8090   # your machine
# Connecting to host.docker.internal:8090 (192.168.65.254:8090)
# remote file exists

blocks.title: Address services by name, never by IP

content.text: Container IPs change. The Compose docs note that Docker assigns them "dynamically from the network's subnet each time a container starts", so "you should always reference services by name, not IP address." Put the name in configuration, such as
, and the same image works on every machine.

blocks.title: Published ports are open beyond your machine by default

content.text: Docker's docs warn that "publishing container ports is insecure by default": a plain
makes the port available "not only to the Docker host, but to the outside world as well." Add
